findings.title: Win, every bench sign-off, the Meeting extension and the pin strike all play the same cheer/jingle, and two jingles overlap at the last station step
findings.room: all (arcade, garage, qfn, observatory, spectrum, meeting, playground)
findings.problem: There is one celebration cue in the game. `Sound.cheer()` (src/render/audio.ts:73) is `jingle()` (audio.ts:75) followed by four coworker 'cheer' voices. Game.win() fires it (src/game.ts:350). The same cue also fires for every bench sign-off: arcade sign-off src/stations/arcade/station.ts:275, garage TEST pass garage/station.ts:228, observatory log observatory/station.ts:198, spectrum send spectrum/station.ts:235 and QFN ship qfn/station.ts:285. Mid-job milestones use the bare jingle too: the Meeting extension reel (game.ts:236) and the Playground pin strike (game.ts:347). The hooked audio logs agree. Each of the five arcade cabinets logged the identical 21-oscillator jingle (523/659/784/1047 arpeggio, then a held 523/659/784 chord), a 1319 bell and about 12 cheer syllables. For the 5th cabinet, 'cab5 signoff' carried one jingle and the 'win step' a frame later carried a second full jingle plus a second crowd. QFN showed the same pattern: three identical ship jingles, then the win jingle. Garage: three TEST-pass jingles, then the win jingle. The Meeting coupler-extension attach mid-route logged the exact win jingle. So the player hears the 'job won' sound 4–6 times per station room. The real finish is indistinguishable from a sub-step, and at the final step it is just a louder, muddier double. DR-11 asks that the success moment be the juicy peak. Here it is the 6th repeat of a sound that has stopped meaning anything.
findings.fix:
Make three tiers in src/render/audio.ts:
1. `stepDone()`: the existing objectives bell 1175 (src/ui/objectives.ts:103).
2. `milestone()`: a short two-note up-chime (e.g. bell 784 then 1175, 0.25 s, vol .05) and a single 'hm-cheer' voice. Use it for station sign-off, ship, log and send, the Meeting extension attach and the pin strike.
3. `win()`: a longer fanfare with a low kick or bass hit (sine 110→45 at .15), the arpeggio an octave lower plus a held 5-note chord over 1.8 s, a crowd of 6+ cheer voices, and a short music duck.
Replace `a.cheer()` with `a.milestone()` in the five station files. In Game.win() call `audio.win()` only. Optionally skip the station's milestone when `station.complete()` will be true after this action, so the last step plays only the win.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/juice-audio/arcade.mjs and qfn.mjs. The final step's drain should contain exactly one win signature (the new bass hit) and no 523-1047 jingle in the sign-off drains. tests/station-*.spec.ts still pass.
findings.verify_reason: In src/render/audio.ts:73, cheer() is jingle() plus four cheer voices. It fires from game.ts:350 win() and from every station sign-off line cited (arcade:275, garage:228, qfn:285, observatory:198, spectrum:235). game.ts:236 and :347 call jingle() directly. My own garage run logged three TEST-pass jingles (523/659/784/1047 plus a held chord) and then a fourth at delivered/win. The meeting run logged the full jingle at 'extension F' and again at the win.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:207: the second extension path also calls audio.cheer()
node mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap4-juice-audio/garage.mjs: [TEST pass job1], [job2 pass], [job3 pass -> drive] and [delivered/win] each hold the 523-1047 jingle
node mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap4-juice-audio/meeting.mjs: [extension F] holds plug bells plus the jingle

findings.title: Hitstop exists only for the Playground/Meeting cable plug-in; win, failures, trips, pops and Lunch plug-ins never freeze
findings.fix:
Add a `Game.freeze(s:number)` helper (`this.hitstop=Math.max(this.hitstop,s)`) and call it with these values:
- win(): .12
- Lunch fail (lunch-runtime.ts:285): .15
- breaker trip and short (meeting-strip.ts:82, lunch-runtime.ts:264): .08
- scorch: .06
- arcade trip(), popBlock() and popLed(), garage tripFuse(): .07
- station sign-off, ship, log and send success: .05
- slingshot release (game.ts:256): .06

In lunch-runtime.ts:156 replace `g.audio.plug();g.burst(...)` with `g.audio.plug();g.plugFlash(target.pos)` so Lunch connections match the other cable floors.

Expose `hitstop` in snapshot(). Make drive.advance() honour it, for example by consuming the hitstop before stepping, so a spec can assert `snap().hitstopFired`.
findings.verify: New unit/spec: after the arcade 'power' that trips (tests/station-arcade.spec.ts first cabinet), snapshot reports a hitstop > 0 or a counter incremented. Manual non-?manual play: the frame visibly holds on the TRIP marquee. Lunch plug-in shows the cyan ring and star burst (retake juice-audio-10).
findings.verify_reason: A grep for hitstop/timeScale over src/ finds only game.ts:48, :249 (plugFlash) and :456. lunch-runtime.ts:156 calls g.audio.plug() plus a 12-spark burst with no plugFlash. win(), trips, shorts, the Lunch fail, the arcade and garage fuses and the slingshot (game.ts:256) never set hitstop. DR-11 (mockups/review5/RULES.md:99) asks for hitstop on success and failure moments.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:457: the ?manual branch is skipped, so specs can't see hitstop
findings.fix_correction: Keep drive.advance() free of hitstop, or make it opt-in. Otherwise every ?manual spec that advances right after a trip or win would silently lose sim time. Expose a counter instead, e.g. snapshot().hitstops++, so tests can assert that a hitstop fired.

findings.title: No flash at the win or at any failure: the win is confetti only, and particles are real-time so the frame after the event shows nothing
findings.problem:
Game.win() (src/game.ts:350-351) lights the machine and spawns 90 + 40 confetti. It spawns no 'flash' particle, no ring and no screen flash. The 'flash' particle type (src/render/particles.ts:30, life .18 s) is used only by plugFlash (game.ts:249) and the arcade LED pop (arcade/station.ts:311). Failures have no flash either.
- Lunch spoil (lunch-runtime.ts:285) is six grey puffs at the fridge.
- The Meeting and Lunch trips are 14–18 small sparks at the strip.
- The QFN send-back shows only the problem rings.

In the immediate-frame captures (taken without the 900 ms settle):
- juice-audio-02 (Playground win, +0.15 s): confetti, no burst at the lamp.
- juice-audio-06 (Meeting trip): only a few specks at the strip; the projector and the coworkers show nothing.
- juice-audio-12 (Lunch spoil): the cause is a small sad-face badge at the top of the frame.
- juice-audio-26 (QFN send-back): only pink rings.

DR-11 asks for flash, sound and hitstop together. Without a flash, the failure cause also isn't 'shown in the world first' at a readable size (DR-28).
findings.fix:
1. In Game.win() add `this.burst({x:target.x,y:1.6,z:target.z},'#fff3c8',1,'flash');this.burst({x:target.x,y:.05,z:target.z},'#ffe36e',1,'ring');this.burst(target,'#ffe36e',8,'star')`.
2. Add a CSS full-screen flash: a `.hud-flash` div with opacity 0→.35→0 over 120 ms, white for success and #ff7a6b for failure. Trigger it from Game.win(), lunch-runtime.ts:285, meeting-strip.ts:82, the arcade trip and popBlock, garage tripFuse, and the QFN/observatory/spectrum tier-0 branches. Keep it ≤120 ms near a taught part (DR-79).
3. For the Lunch fail, also add a 'flash' plus an 8-particle dust ring at the fridge or oven position.
findings.verify: Retake juice-audio-02/-06/-12/-26 immediately after the event (page.screenshot with no wait). The flash or ring is visible at the machine and the vignette shows in the frame. Check that DR-79's 120 ms bound holds with two shots 0.1 s apart.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:350-351 win() spawns only confetti (90 + 40). 'flash' is used only at game.ts:249 and arcade/station.ts:311. The Lunch fail (lunch-runtime.ts:285) is smoke puffs only. My immediate Meeting trip shot shows only a few sparks and dust at the strip. Nothing lights up at the projector or the coworkers.

findings.title: Pip does the victory dance when Lunch fails (spoil/burn), and the camera never looks at the fridge or oven
findings.fix:
1. Add `failed=false` to Game. In lunch-runtime.ts:285 set `g.failed=true` alongside won, and set `g.winAt=performance.now()` with `g.winFocus` pointing at the fail spot `at`.
2. In PipRig.update take a `failed` flag. Use a slump pose: arms down and slightly forward (lx=rx≈-.3), head pitch +.35 (looking down), no bounce, and one squash of .3. Optionally play a head-shake (yaw sin(t*10)*.25 for 0.6 s).
3. Stop the face-camera turn at game.ts:407 when failed, or turn Pip toward the fail spot instead.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/juice-audio/lunch.mjs part C. In juice-audio-12, Pip is slumped (arms below shoulders), and the fridge sits inside the centre 70% of the frame together with Pip before the card drops.
findings.verify_reason: lunch-runtime.ts:285 sets g.won=true on failure. game.ts:411 passes won:this.won to the rig, and pipRig.ts:57/77/88 apply the bounce, arms overhead and head-up pose. winAt stays 0, so there's no push-in (game.ts:369), and game.ts:407 turns Pip to the camera. My reproduction (verify-12) shows Pip in the power room with both arms raised. The fridge is a tiny sad-face badge at the top edge.

findings.title: Lunch water short plays the success plug chime and ticks 'Mop up the leak' and 'Power the feed post' as done, while Supply B is tripped and the puddle is still there
findings.problem:
I plugged the thick cable into the kitchen feed post through the unmopped leak, the documented short case. The audio log shows the full `plug()` success chime (two highpass clicks plus the rising 880/1109/1319 bells) and, in the same frame, the trip/short sound (75 Hz square plus lowpass noise). Two objective step-done bells (1175) follow.

The card in juice-audio-11 has moved to step 4, 'Keep the oven on until the tray is baked', with three dots green. The puddle is still on the floor, a red lightning-bolt scar sits at the leak, and Supply B is tripped (`tripped:true`, event `short`).

The cause is `kitchenFed` (src/ui/objectives.ts:19). It only checks that some cable has the 'kitchen' port, `lead.closed` and not `dead`. It doesn't check that the source is live or that the oven is on. Steps 2 and 3 (objectives.ts:43-44) both accept kitchenFed, and steps latch forever (objectives.ts:101-103). So a short teaches 'that worked', with two success chimes and a skipped step. The leak step will never come back even after the player resets the breaker into the same puddle.

This breaks DR-28 (the failure cause shown first) and DR-47 (state shown truthfully). The success and failure sounds collide on one event.
evidence: juice-audio/lunch.mjs log [plug thick through leak -> SHORT]: plug bells, s75 + Nlowpass300, then s1175 x2
findings.fix:
1. Change kitchenFed to require a live feed: `c.ports.includes('kitchen')&&c.lead.closed&&!c.lead.dead&&g.lunch.circuit.loads.find(l=>l.id==='oven')?.state==='on'`. Alternatively check that the cable's source port isn't tripped.
2. Make step 2 ('Mop up the leak') depend only on water<.1 or a bridge being present over the leak, not on kitchenFed.
3. In lunch-runtime.ts:156, play only the mechanical click at connect (`noise` ×2, no bells). Play the bell part one circuit step later, and only if no trip or short event fired for that source. Otherwise let the trip sound stand alone.
findings.verify: Extend tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts 'a live cable through the leak shorts and trips the supply until reset' with: after the short, `.objective` still shows the leak step, and the done-dot count is unchanged. Re-run juice-audio/lunch.mjs: the [SHORT] drain contains no 880/1109/1319 bells and no 1175 step bells.
findings.verify_reason: objectives.ts:19 kitchenFed checks only ports/closed/!dead. A short trips the source (electrical.ts:23) but leaves lead.closed true (lunch-runtime.ts:245). My run's [plug thick through leak -> SHORT] drain held the plug chime (Nhighpass3200/2600 + 880/1109/1319), then s75 + Nlowpass300, then two s1175 step bells. Supply b was tripped with event 'short'. verify-11 shows step 4 'Keep the oven on…' with 3 green dots, and the puddle and the bolt scar are still there.

findings.title: The same sound is used for different faults: overload trip = water short, arcade PTC trip = garage dead short, and every bench 'doesn't work' is one 160 Hz buzz
findings.room: meeting, lunch, arcade, garage, observatory, spectrum, qfn
findings.problem:
The audio palette doesn't separate fault types, so sound can't teach what went wrong (DR-28, DR-47).
- The Meeting overload trip (src/meeting-strip.ts:82) is byte-identical to the Lunch overload trip and the Lunch water short. lunch-runtime.ts:264 handles both `trip` and `short` in one branch: `tone(75,.25,.1,'square')` plus `noise(.25,.1,300)`. Logs: Meeting [projector E -> TRIP] gives s75@.1 and Nlowpass300@.1. Lunch [SHORT] gives the same pair. An overloaded breaker and a short through water are opposite lessons (too many loads vs. a low-resistance path), yet they sound the same.
- The arcade PTC trip (arcade/station.ts:290: noise bandpass 1800 plus 120 Hz square .35 s plus groan) is the same as the garage dead-short fuse (garage/station.ts:238: noise bandpass 1800 plus 120 Hz square .3 s plus groan). Logs: arcade [FUSE TRIP] and garage [FUSE SHORT] match.
- Every tier-0 verdict uses `tone(160,.25,.06,'square')` plus `voice('groan',1)`: garage TEST fail (garage/station.ts:225), observatory log (observatory/station.ts:195), spectrum send (spectrum/station.ts:231) and QFN CHECK (qfn/station.ts:281). This covers a spike reset, a weak signal, a missed pad and a bad layout alike.
- Beyond the trip itself there is no 'machine powering down' sound. The projector, kettle and heater in Meeting, and the oven and lamps in Lunch, go dark silently.
evidence: juice-audio meeting.mjs, lunch.mjs, arcade.mjs, garage.mjs logs
findings.fix:
Add named fault cues in src/render/audio.ts and use them at the call sites:
- `breakerTrip()`: a heavy clack (lowpass noise 300 at .1), then a descending 'power-down' whirr (sawtooth 220→55 over .6 s, lowpass 800, vol .05) for each load that drops.
- `short()`: a sharp zap/crackle (highpass noise 4000 .08 s at .14, plus 3 random 2–3 kHz square blips over 0.15 s), and with water a hiss (highpass 6000 noise .5 s at .04).
- `ptcTrip()`: a tick plus a rising thermal hum, distinct from the garage `fuseBang()`.
- `verdictFail(kind)`: pitch or timbre per kind (reset = robot 'bonk' sweep, weak = falling sine, layout = double buzz).

In lunch-runtime.ts:264 branch on event.kind ('short' → short(), 'trip' → breakerTrip()). Use breakerTrip() in meeting-strip.ts:82.
findings.verify: Re-run the juice-audio scripts. Meeting trip, Lunch short and Lunch overload (thin cable to oven plus fridge) produce three different signatures, and arcade and garage fuse logs differ. A blind listen test: name the fault from the sound alone.
findings.verify_reason: meeting-strip.ts:82 and lunch-runtime.ts:264 both play tone(75,.25,.1,'square') + noise(.25,.1,300). Lunch uses one branch for 'trip' and 'short'. Arcade trip at :290 (bandpass1800 + 120 Hz square .35) and garage tripFuse at :238 (bandpass1800 + 120 Hz square .3) are near-identical. Tier-0 verdicts at garage:225, observatory:195, spectrum:232 and qfn:281 all use tone(160,.25,.06,'square'). My logs match: Meeting TRIP gives s75@.1 + Nlowpass300@.1, the same as Lunch SHORT, and garage FUSE SHORT gives Nbandpass1800@.12 + s120@.06.
extra_evidence: verify-gap4-juice-audio meeting.mjs [projector E -> TRIP] and lunch.mjs [SHORT] logs

findings.title: Lunch's job-ending failure is the quietest cue in the game, the fridge never warns audibly across 120 s, and spoil and burn sound alike
findings.problem:
The fail sting at src/lunch-runtime.ts:285 is `tone(120,.7,.05,'triangle')`: peak gain .05 on a 120 Hz triangle, falling to 60 Hz. That is about the level of grabbing a mug (`pop()`: sine 320 at .05 plus triangle 520 at .03), quieter than a footstep-adjacent thud, and far below the slingshot (.12) or a breaker trip (.1). At low frequency on laptop speakers it is nearly inaudible. Three bandpassed groans at .06 follow.

During the 120 s spoil wait the logs show no fridge warning sound at all. Only one alarm voice is heard just before the fail ([wait 120s] contains only coworker syllables and the final t120). The oven has a beep warning from 60 s (lunch-runtime.ts:282); the fridge has nothing.

Spoil and burn use the identical sting. The fail card (`failed()`, src/ui/game-ui.ts:224-227) lands with no sound, while the win card gets a thud and a bell (game-ui.ts:219-220).

The only way to lose a job ends on a murmur. A player looking elsewhere (the fridge is often off-screen, juice-audio-12) misses the cause entirely (DR-11, DR-28).
findings.fix:
1. Add a fridge warning. From temperature ≥ .7, play a compressor stutter (two lowpass 200 noise bursts) every 4 s from the fridge position, and from ≥ .9 a 660 Hz double beep every 2 s. Mirror the oven code at lunch-runtime.ts:282.
2. Add `audio.fail(kind)`: a 'sad trombone' of 3–4 descending notes (square or saw through lowpass 1200: 392, 370, 349, 294 at .09, .25 s each).
   - spoil: add a fridge door clunk (lowpass noise 250 at .1);
   - burn: add a sizzle (highpass noise 3000, .8 s, at .06).
3. In failed() (game-ui.ts:224) play a card thud like the result card.
findings.verify: Re-run juice-audio/lunch.mjs. Fridge warning cues appear in the 90–120 s drain, the SPOIL drain contains a sting with peak ≥ .09 and a spoil-specific cue, and the card drain contains a thud.
findings.verify_reason: lunch-runtime.ts:285 plays only tone(120,.7,.05,'triangle') plus delayed groans. My [wait 120s] drain held just two alarm syllables and t120@0.050, with no fridge warning cue in 120 s. The oven warning beep is at :282. My card drain ([spoil +1.5s]) held only groan syllables and no thud. failed() is at game-ui.ts:232-236 (not 224-227) and plays no sound. The result card's thud is at :219.

findings.title: Garage delivery payoff plays a ~22-per-second machine-gun beep: the test-cycle animation keeps running under the drive
findings.problem:
On the third TEST pass, startDrive() is called (src/stations/garage/station.ts:230 → :256) while the 5-cycle test animation is still running (`cycleT>=0`, started by `kick(v,s,true)` a moment earlier).

Each frame:
1. The drive sets `this.motorOn=d<ROUTE_LEN?1:0` (station.ts:364), i.e. 1.
2. The cycle branch (station.ts:367-369) stores `before=this.motorOn` (1), then sets motorOn from the cycle phase.
3. In every 'off' sub-phase, and after the last cycle until c ≥ cycles+2, `!this.motorOn&&before` is true, so `land(true)` fires every frame.
4. land() ends in `this.game.audio.tone(320,.25,.03,'sine')` (station.ts:397) and resets the current-pulse flow.

The hooked log [driving] holds 135 copies of s320@0.030 in about 6 s of sim, plus more in [job2 pass] and [job3 pass -> drive]. The robot's victory drive, the room's payoff, is accompanied by a buzzing stutter. The pulses on the board also restart every frame. The delivery itself has only a single 1568 bell (station.ts:364) before the win jingle.
findings.fix:
1. In startDrive() set `this.cycleT=-1;this.kickT=-1;` before driving starts. Alternatively, guard the cycle branch with `if(this.cycleT>=0&&!this.driving)`.
2. In land(), early-return when `this.driving`.
3. Give the drive its own cue: a soft motor whirr (sawtooth 90 Hz through lowpass 500 at .02, gain following motorOn) and a 'docked' clunk plus chime at DRIVE_TIME.
findings.verify: Re-run juice-audio/garage.mjs. The [driving] drain contains no repeated s320 cues (at most 1). tests/station-garage.spec.ts still passes with delivered=true.
findings.verify_reason: The code path holds. Drive sets motorOn=1 each frame (garage/station.ts:364) before the cycle branch (:367), and the cycle started at TEST (:223) is still running. So in every off sub-phase, and for 1.2 s after the last cycle, `!motorOn&&before` calls land() each frame, and land() plays tone(320,.25,.03) at :397. My run's [driving] drain was 135 cues, about 132 of them s320@0.030, with only 3 voice syllables besides. verify-24 shows the win confetti at the bench.
extra_evidence: The [pulse ok] and [job2 pass] drains also contain long s320 runs, so land() repeats outside the drive too (likely the same before/after pattern while kickT runs). Check animateKick/kick paths as well

findings.title: Meeting: the breaker trip draws no coworker reaction, while the correct fix (unplugging the kettle) draws three groans
findings.problem:
At the trip (src/meeting-strip.ts:82), `g.alarm(at,4)` is centred on the strip at the boardroom door. The boardroom coworkers sit beyond 4 m, so no alarm voice fires. The hooked log [projector E -> TRIP] contains only the switch click, s75 square and lowpass noise: no voice. The projector simply stays dark (juice-audio-06).

Unplugging the kettle or heater (meeting-strip.ts:68-70) calls `g.alarm({x:12,z:-5.5},6)` and three `voice('groan')` (log [unplug heater/kettle]: 11 groan syllables). So the room's loudest negative feedback, the social 'boo', lands on the right action, and the actual fault gets silence.

In a game that teaches by doing, the player learns 'unplugging was wrong'. The trip, which is what should feel like a failure the player caused and understood, reads as nothing happening (DR-28, DR-04 pattern).
evidence: juice-audio/meeting.mjs log [projector E -> TRIP] and [unplug heater/kettle]
findings.fix:
1. On trip, call `g.alarm({x:12,z:-5.5},6)` and two `voice('groan')`. Flicker the boardroom pendant and the projector screen off with a CRT 'thunk' (sine 60 Hz .2 s plus highpass 5000 tick), and play the power-down whirr from the previous finding.
2. On unplug, replace the three groans with a single `voice('hm')`, keeping the comedy but softer. Then, if the gauge drops below the breaker limit, play a small confirm tick (bell 988 at .03) at the strip.
findings.verify: Re-run juice-audio/meeting.mjs. The TRIP drain contains coworker groan syllables, and the unplug drain has ≤ 3 syllables plus the confirm tick. tests/routes.spec.ts switchProjector still sees alarmed ≥ 1.
findings.verify_reason: My meeting run's [projector E -> TRIP] drain held only Nhighpass2500, s420, s75 and Nlowpass300, with no voice syllables. alarm(at,4) at meeting-strip.ts:82 doesn't reach the boardroom NPCs. The [unplug heater/kettle] drain held an alarm voice plus 9 groan syllables (meeting-strip.ts:68-70). verify-06 shows only small sparks at the strip.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:137-138 (alarm voices only NPCs inside radius)

findings.title: Placing any part on a bench plays the full 'plug seated' success chime, even a wrong part that will trip the fuse
findings.problem:
`plug()` (src/render/audio.ts:60) is the click-clack plus rising 880/1109/1319 arpeggio, the game's 'connection made' reward. The arcade plays it on every block placed in the chain or across the LED (arcade/station.ts:259, :264). The garage plays it on every part fitted to a slot (garage/station.ts:205). Logs: the arcade 'fix + fuse cools' and each cabinet drain carry 1–2 plug chimes. Garage 'fit diode, flip' carries one for a flipped diode about to cause a dead short.

So a reversed or across-the-LED part is greeted with the success chime. The chime is the most frequent positive cue in station rooms, which dilutes the real connection and success moments. Sound should never praise the action that's about to fail (DR-28, DR-38).
findings.fix: Add `seat()`: two highpass clicks only (noise .02 at 3200/2600, vol .06), no bells. Use it in the bench slot handlers. Keep `plug()` for live cable connections and objects docking (robot on stand, tray to bench, Lunch ports).
findings.verify: Re-run arcade.mjs and garage.mjs. Slot actions log only the two Nhighpass clicks, with no 880/1109/1319 bells.
findings.verify_reason: audio.ts:60 plug() is the click-clack plus 880/1109/1319 bells. It's called on slot placement at arcade:259/264, garage:205 and observatory:179. My garage [fit diode, flip] drain contains the full plug chime for the diode that then dead-shorts.
extra_evidence: src/stations/observatory/station.ts:179 also uses a.plug() for knob slots

findings.title: QFN send-back is nearly silent and nothing physical happens to the board
findings.problem:
Shipping a bad board (src/stations/qfn/station.ts:283) only calls `a.voice('groan',1)` and `g.alarm()`. There is no tone, thud or buzzer, and no particle. The hooked log [SHIP scrambled: SEND BACK] contains just three bandpassed groan syllables. It is quieter than the CHECK button's own fail tone (log [CHECK on bad board]: s160 square at .06, qfn:281).

Visually (juice-audio-26), problem rings appear and a toast fades in. The board doesn't move, and nothing 'comes back from test'. The ship success, by contrast, gets the full jingle, crowd and confetti. The room's only failure is its least felt moment, so the 'No board sent back' bonus (qfn:77) has no sting to avoid.
findings.verify: Re-run juice-audio/qfn.mjs. The SEND BACK drain contains the thunk and buzzer. An immediate screenshot shows the board offset or dropping and the rings flashing.
findings.verify_reason: qfn/station.ts:283 tier-0 ship only calls say, voice('groan'), alarm, showMarks and redraw. It plays no tone or noise and makes no particle or board motion. The CHECK fail at :281 does play the s160 buzz. I checked this in code and did not reproduce it live.

findings.title: Sign-off swaps in the next cabinet or board in the same frame, so there's no visual beat at the bench
findings.verify: Immediate screenshot after signoff shows the solved board and a PASS stamp, and the next job appears ≥ 1 s later. The station-*.spec.ts timings need a wait of ≥ 1.2 s after signoff.
findings.verify_reason: arcade/station.ts:271-278 records the verdict, fires cheer, then index++, powerOff, the next setup and showJob, all in the same call. juice-audio-15 (viewed) already shows cabinet 2/5 RHYTHM (3.3 V, 47 Ω), and the only praise is the toast 'Pinball bumper: Elegant ★'. Garage :229 and QFN :287 swap the same way. QFN at least plays dropIn() for the next board.

findings.title: Music never reacts to win, fail or pause, and seven of ten rooms reuse the Playground loop
findings.problem:
`schedule()` and `playStep()` (src/render/audio.ts:83-86) check only `isMuted`. Nothing ducks, stops, filters or changes the music bus on win, on fail, or while paused. togglePause (src/game.ts:191) only zeroes the strain hum. The win jingle and the Lunch groans therefore compete with the same jaunty loop, and the fail moment keeps upbeat swing music running under the 'sad' beat.

SONGS (audio.ts:6-10) defines only playground, meeting and lunch. setLevel falls back to playground (audio.ts:30), so the lobby, arcade, arcade-rush, garage, qfn, observatory and spectrum all play the Playground song.
findings.fix:
1. Add `duck(level,secs)` on musicBus.gain using setTargetAtTime.
   - win: duck to .12 for 2.5 s under the fanfare, then resume.
   - fail: lowpass the bus to 400 Hz and pitch the next bars down, or stop the loop.
   - pause: duck to .25.
2. Add at least a hub song and one 'bench' song shared by the stations (a slower bpm 84, sparse vibraphone).
findings.verify: Probe musicBus gain via the hook (log gain value at win+0.3 s and fail+0.3 s). Expect a value below .2.
findings.verify_reason: audio.ts:6-10 defines only the playground, meeting and lunch songs. setLevel (:30) falls back to playground. schedule() and playStep() (:83-86+) check only isMuted. togglePause (game.ts:191) only calls strain(0). Nothing touches musicBus after start (:25).

findings.title: Cable-wrap knock spams 6–10 times a second while dragging or after a slingshot
findings.fix:
1. Knock only when bends increase and the new bend is a different obstacle than the last one knocked.
2. Rate-limit to one knock per 0.3 s (store lastKnock time) and skip knocks while the rope speed is below a threshold.
3. Play the unwrap as a softer 'slip' (bandpass noise 1500 at .02) at most once per 0.5 s.
findings.verify: Re-run juice-audio/playground.mjs. The slingshot aftermath logs ≤ 3 knocks, and one wrap around a pillar still logs exactly one knock.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:284 knocks on any change in bend count, in either direction. In my meeting run the [walk] leg after the extension had 9 knocks (t190/t285 + Nbandpass2400) and [coupler F] had 5.

findings.title: Win confetti and the push-in centre on level.target, which in the Garage is the bench, not the delivered robot
findings.problem: Game.win() bursts 90 confetti at `this.level.target` (src/game.ts:351). For station rooms the target is the bench, so in the Garage the win confetti erupts over the bench. The thing that succeeded, the robot that just drove to the dock, sits at the far-left edge, cut by the frame (juice-audio-24). The garage's own 20-confetti burst at the robot (garage/station.ts:364) fires 1.4 s earlier with only a single bell. The machine coming to life isn't where the celebration is.
findings.fix: Let a station provide `winSpot()` (for the garage, the robot's dock position). Use it in Game.win() for the confetti and for winFocus. Move the bell, confetti, a 'flash' and the jingle to the same frame, at the dock.
findings.verify: Retake the garage win shot immediately after won. The confetti and the robot are inside the centre 70% of the frame with Pip.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:351 bursts 90 confetti at level.target. The garage's own delivery burst is at the robot (station.ts:364). juice-audio-24 (viewed) shows the confetti fountain over the bench, with Pip at the bench and the route area off-centre.

findings.title: Mute works and persists, but its label never changes, and reduced-motion silently drops the result-card sound
findings.problem:
Mute is solid. Clicking [data-ui=sound] set localStorage 'circuit-crew-muted'='1'. After a reload, aria-pressed was 'true' and the icon swapped (Sound constructor at src/render/audio.ts:14-17, syncSound at src/ui/game-ui.ts:142-143). The label stays 'Mute audio' in both states, though (src/ui/screens.ts:103, :158; syncSound doesn't update aria-label), so a screen reader announces 'Mute audio, pressed'.

Separately, the result-card thud sound is wrapped in `if(!reduced())` (game-ui.ts:219). Players who prefer reduced motion lose an audio cue, which is unrelated to motion.
evidence: juice-audio/playground.mjs log: 'muted after click 1 Mute audio', 'after reload {ls:1, pressed:true}'
findings.fix:
1. In syncSound set `b.setAttribute('aria-label',muted?'Unmute audio':'Mute audio')`, and update the tile `<span>` text to 'Sound off' when muted.
2. In game-ui.ts:219 play the thud regardless of reduced(), applying only the `.thud` CSS class conditionally.
findings.verify: Re-run the mute section of juice-audio/playground.mjs. The label reads 'Unmute audio' after the click and after a reload. With emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}) the result drain still contains the Nlowpass thud.
findings.verify_reason: syncSound (game-ui.ts:142-143) updates aria-pressed, the class and the icon, but not aria-label. screens.ts:103 and :158 hard-code 'Mute audio', and the tile span reads 'Sound'. game-ui.ts:219 wraps the thud audio in if(!reduced()).
findings.fix_correction: With aria-pressed kept, the WAI-ARIA toggle pattern prefers a fixed label: 'Mute audio, pressed' is correct. Either keep aria-label fixed (then only the visible tile text should change) or drop aria-pressed and swap the label. Don't do both. The reduced-motion thud part stands.

notes.fun:
I logged the event-to-sound table live, by hooking WebAudio: OscillatorNode and BufferSource start, routed back to the sfx bus.

Sounds by event:
- **Plug-in** (Playground/Meeting): plug() click-clack plus 880/1109/1319 bells, plus plugFlash (.09 s hitstop, flash, ring, stars). This is the only juicy beat.
- **Lunch plug-in:** plug() only, with no hitstop or flash.
- **Unplug:** pop(), the same as grabbing any prop. Meeting appliance unplug: pop plus highpass click plus 3 groans.
- **Breaker trip** (Meeting and Lunch): 75 Hz square plus lowpass noise, small shake. Lunch water short: identical.
- **Arcade PTC trip:** bandpass-1800 noise, 120 Hz square, groan. Garage dead-short fuse: the same.
- **LED pop:** bandpass-2600 noise, 90 Hz square, groan, plus a flash.
- **Block pop:** noise, pop, 150 Hz saw, alarm voice, plus debris and smoke.
- **Lunch spoil/burn:** 120 Hz triangle at .05 plus 3 groans, identical for both.
- **Scorch:** 60 Hz saw.
- **Slingshot release:** 90 Hz saw at .12 plus noise plus shake, no hitstop.
- **Prop break:** glass, clatter or thud by mass.
- **Coworker alarm:** formant voice, rate-limited to 0.5 s.
- **Step tick:** bell 1175.
- **Win:** cheer(), i.e. jingle plus crowd. The result card adds a thud plus a 90 Hz triangle, and a bell if improved.
- **Fail card:** silent.
- **Bench sign-off, ship, log, send:** the same cheer() plus bell 1319.
- **Send-back:** a groan only.
- **Lobby locked door:** 140 Hz square.
- **Lobby door enter:** a pop that the instant location.href cuts off.
- **Footsteps:** not observable under ?manual.

What works: the plug-in beat (click, chime, hitstop, flash, ring), the strain hum and creak, coworker gibberish, and the result-card thud and count-up all feel good. The procedural palette is coherent.

What is missing: escalation and contrast. There is one celebration sound for everything, hitstop only on the plug, no flash at the win, and fault sounds shared across different faults. Failures are quieter than successes: the QFN send-back and the Lunch spoil are the quietest events in their rooms. Lunch fail even plays Pip's victory dance.
notes.playability:
Mute persists across reloads and jobs (localStorage 'circuit-crew-muted'), and the icon and aria-pressed sync on load. Only the aria-label is static.

The AudioContext correctly waits for a user gesture: the first click or key starts it (audio.ts:21, game-ui.ts:45). Hitstop skips the sim step in frame() but not in ?manual, so no spec can test it. Particles update on real time in render() (game.ts:438), so a review screenshot taken with cap.mjs's 900 ms settle never shows spark or flash bursts. Juice shots must be taken immediately.

The garage drive bug (a 22 Hz beep stutter) is a real code defect, with a one-line fix (cycleT=-1 in startDrive).

No console or page errors in any run: playground, meeting, lunch ×2, arcade ×2, garage, qfn, lobby.
notes.teaching:
Sound currently can't teach fault types. Overload and water short are the same cue, and every bench tier-0 verdict is the same 160 Hz buzz plus groan.

Worse, the Lunch water short plays the success plug chime and two objective-done bells. It latches 'Mop up the leak' as done while the puddle remains and the supply is tripped, so the player is told the wrong lesson.

In Meeting the social feedback is inverted: the trip is unremarked, and the correct unplug is booed. Bench placements praise every part with the success chime, including the reversed diode about to short.

The positives: the Meeting/Lunch trip has an in-world spark at the strip or supply. The arcade pops have debris, smoke and a flash at the right part. The garage reboot has stars, red eyes and an alarm voice at the robot. These follow DR-28's 'cue at the part' well, and only their sound design needs separating.
notes.clarity:
Success and failure moments lack the DR-11 trio.

| Moment | Flash | Sound | Hitstop |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cable plug-in (Playground/Meeting) | yes | yes | yes |
| Win | confetti only | generic jingle | no |
| Any failure | no | yes | no |

Immediate-frame captures confirm it: juice-audio-02 (win), -06 (trip), -12 (spoil) and -26 (send-back). Each frame shows at most a few specks. The Lunch fail frame keeps the camera on a cheering Pip, with the fridge far up-frame. The station sign-off instantly swaps in the next board, so the solve has no visible beat at the bench camera.
notes.models: Not in scope for this gap-fill. Note only that the win and fail beats would benefit from a slumped Pip pose (none exists, and pipRig only has a won pose) and a power-down state on devices (projector screen, oven lamp). Those are animation and state assets, not meshes.

rechecked: LR4 (Lunch in-world fail beat before the card): still present (alarm, 6 puffs, 3 groans, 1.2 s hold, lunch-runtime.ts:285-286). The beat is weak: a quiet sting, no flash or hitstop, no camera on the cause, and Pip does the win dance. Filed as new findings, not a regression.

A10 (confetti through the bench camera): FIXED. The shared cheer() goes off behind the table (juice-audio-15 shows no confetti over the bench); the side effect is that the sign-off has no visible celebration.
L6 (Tab/R only during play): not regressed in my runs. The fail card's Retry is shown with an R hint (juice-audio-13).
Mute persistence: works (localStorage, aria-pressed restored after reload). Only the label is static.
QA 10 / DR-11 framing: not re-filed. Arcade win (juice-audio-18) still crops Pip at the bottom-left edge, consistent with earlier framing findings.
DR-80: g.close() returned [] for every run (playground ×2, meeting, lunch ×2, arcade ×2, garage, qfn, lobby).
